fixes.explanation: Close, but the psalm flips it. Verse 4 says, "He chooses our inheritance for us…" So God does the choosing, not the people. Think of it like a batch where someone else already picked the cookie shape for you.
False is right, baker! Verse 4 says, "He chooses our inheritance for us…" God does the choosing, not the people. Nobody is standing there with a clipboard picking their own.
He loves him! Verse 4 says, "He chooses our inheritance for us, the pride of Jacob, whom He loves." Love is the word the psalm uses. It sits right there in the verse.

Angry isn't in this verse, friend. Verse 4 says, "He chooses our inheritance for us, the pride of Jacob, whom He loves." The word the psalm uses for how He feels is love, and that's the opposite of angry. It's a good word, and it sits right next to the inheritance.
Shouts of joy, baker! Verse 5 says, "God has ascended amid shouts of joy, the LORD with the sound of the horn." Joy all around, and a horn blowing too. That's a sound I'd want to hear.
Fear doesn't show up in this verse. Verse 5 says, "God has ascended amid shouts of joy…" The sound around Him is joy, friend, and loud joy at that.

True! Verse 8 says, "God reigns over the nations; God is seated on His holy throne." The psalm gives us a picture of a King who is seated and reigning. That's the picture, baker, right there in the verse.

Moses, the man God sent to bring Israel out of Egypt (Exodus 3:10), is a big name, and I see why you reached for him. But verse 9 says the nobles "…have assembled as the people of the God of Abraham…" The psalm names Abraham here, not Moses.
Elijah was a prophet (1 Kings 18:36), but he isn't in this verse. Verse 9 says the nobles "…have assembled as the people of the God of Abraham…" Abraham is the name the psalm picks.
The nobles are in the verse, so I get it. But verse 9 says the nobles have assembled, and then, "for the shields of the earth belong to God…" The shields are God's, not theirs.
